verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own environments feature (dev, staging, production) lets flags be enabled and toggled per environment, so changes can be tested outside production. A hands-on probe also booted a disposable local self-hosted instance and completed a flag create-and-evaluate loop. However, nothing documents isolation of production data itself (e.g., separate experiment or metric data per environment), and custom environments appear only on a higher pricing tier. missing for 10: documented data isolation between sandbox and production, an explicit sandbox/test mode for agent-driven changes, custom environments on all tiers, independent corroboration of environment-based testing workflows

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: Use environments such as dev, staging, and production to enable or disable feature flags independently.
Feature flags can be enabled and disabled on a per-environment basis.
automate it (for example, from a deploy script) with the toggle feature endpoint, which switches a flag on or off in one or more environments.
a real flag create-and-evaluate loop with no account or license
